report.summary: About 12% of transfers returned 500 and the tail latency reached seconds. This coincides with ledger_app sessions blocked behind an idle-in-transaction session. Outbox delivery and pool capacity look healthy.

findings.claim: Transfers show 81 of 680 requests returning 500 (11.9%), with p95 2.0s and p99 3.45s.
findings.reason: Request metrics directly show the server-error ratio and latency tail.

findings.claim: ledger_app sessions were blocked for up to ~2s behind session 60986, which was idle in transaction, from 16:13:36 to 16:15:02.
findings.reason: Blocker samples name the same idle-in-transaction blocker across three blocked sessions in 10, 21 and 16 samples.

findings.claim: Committed transfers dipped to about 21-28 per 10s bucket during the blocking period, versus a steady 34 outside it. This is consistent with lock waits stalling or failing transfers.
findings.reason: The arrivals dip lines up in time with the blocking window, but no direct link to the 500s was observed.

findings.claim: The outbox consumer and connection pool are not the bottleneck.
findings.reason: All 598 deliveries succeeded in about 71ms, with 0 pool acquisition timeouts and 0 pending borrowers.

limitations: The 500 error messages and stack traces were not observed, so the link between lock waits and the 500s is inferred from timing.
Blocker sampling is every 2s, and the owner and statement of idle session 60986 are not identified.
next_checks: Identify the application or session behind pid 60986 and its open transaction, and find why it stays idle in transaction.
Correlate 500 responses with lock-wait or statement-timeout errors in the application logs.

alternatives.reason: There were 0 acquisition timeouts, pending was 0, and active peaked at 5 of 10.
alternatives.hypothesis: Pool exhaustion caused the 500s and slow requests.

alternatives.reason: All deliveries succeeded with ~71ms latency and no failures.
